standards.rule: Every model version names an owning team and an on-call rotation.
standards.why: Someone has to answer when it misbehaves at 03:00.

standards.rule: Every model version records the pipeline run, the code commit, the data snapshot hash and its parameters.
standards.why: A model that cannot be rebuilt cannot be debugged or audited.

standards.rule: Every production model passed every block gate, or carries an unexpired waiver for the one it did not.
standards.why: Gates are the definition of done; a waiver makes an exception visible and temporary.

standards.rule: Every production model has a model card with intended use, training window, metrics per market and known limits.
A production ranker is at most 3 days old; a production tower at most 14 days.
standards.why: Second-hand inventory turns over fast; a stale model ranks a catalogue that no longer exists.

standards.rule: Every production model has a rollback target still loaded (profile in the Vespa package, version in Triton).
standards.why: Rolling back must be a routing change that takes seconds, not a redeploy.

standards.rule: Every production model passed score parity and skew on staging against the live catalogue.
Every production model has a skew and drift check that ran in the last 24 hours.
